html:
The Union of Lublin was signed on 1 July 1569 at a joint parliament in Lublin, turning the personal union of Poland and Lithuania into one state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

The two lands had shared rulers since the Union of Krewo of 1385. The childless last Jagiellonian king, Sigismund II Augustus, pushed for a firmer union. Lithuania, under pressure from Muscovy, gave in, and lost its Ukrainian lands to the Polish crown. The new state had one elected king and one parliament, the Sejm, but kept separate armies, treasuries and laws. Its nobles, about a tenth of the people, enjoyed wide freedoms. It lasted until the partitions of the late 1700s, and its spread of Polish landlords into Ukraine helped cause the Cossack rising of 1648.
sum: The Union of Lublin was signed on 1 July 1569 at a joint parliament in Lublin, turning the personal union of Poland and Lithuania into one state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
